title: Birth, marriage and death
subtitle: was born, got married, died
summary: Talk about the big moments in a life - being born, getting married and dying - with the right words and prepositions.

lesson.heading: Birth
lesson.text: When a woman has a child, we say she **had a baby**. For the child we use **was born** - always with the verb *be*, and usually in the past.

examples.note: weigh = to be a number of kilograms

examples.text: They are going to call him John, **after** his grandfather.
examples.note: after = with the same name as

lesson.heading: Are you married?
rows: You do not have a partner.
You have a husband or a wife.
Your husband or wife has died.
You and your partner do not live together any more.

lesson.heading: The wedding
lesson.text: On her wedding day a woman is the **bride** and a man is the **groom** (or bridegroom). Two people **get married**, and after the wedding they go on their **honeymoon**.

examples.note: married without got is more formal

examples.text: They went on their **honeymoon** to Italy.

lesson.heading: Death
lesson.text: When a person **dies**, the family and friends go to the **funeral**. Be careful: **die** is the verb, **dead** is the adjective and **death** is the noun.

examples.text: Then Harry became **ill**. He **died** last year.

examples.wrong: Harry is died / Harry is death

lesson.heading: die, dead, death
rows: Her grandmother has been dead for five years now.
His death made her very sad.
All the family came to the funeral.

lesson.text: Two little prepositions to remember: you get married **to** somebody, and you die **of** an illness.

exercises.explanation: We say have a baby, not get a baby.
We say was born or were born - always the past of be.

exercises.prompt: On her wedding day a woman is the ___.
exercises.explanation: The bride is the woman who is getting married.

exercises.prompt: On his wedding day a man is the ___.
exercises.explanation: The man who is getting married is the groom or bridegroom.

exercises.prompt: Match each word with its meaning.

pairs.right: your husband or wife has died
a service for a dead person

exercises.prompt: In 2003 Anne got married ___ Daniel Smith.
exercises.explanation: You get married to someone, not with someone.

exercises.prompt: Daniel's grandmother died ___ old age soon after their wedding.
exercises.explanation: You die of an illness or of old age.

exercises.prompt: Daniel and Anne were ___ their honeymoon when she died.
exercises.explanation: We go on a honeymoon and we are on our honeymoon.

exercises.prompt: Anne's baby daughter was ___ two years later. They called her Lydia, after Daniel's grandmother.
exercises.explanation: A baby is born - we always use be + born.

exercises.answer: Christopher Columbus was born in 1451 and died in 1506.
exercises.explanation: was born for the start of a life, died for the end.
Harry is dead. With be we use the adjective dead, not died.

exercises.prompt: Kelly's grandmother has been ___ for five years now.
exercises.explanation: After be we use the adjective dead.

exercises.prompt: Put each word or phrase into the right part of life.
